Photosynthesis

What is Photosynthesis?

Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy, usually from the sun, into chemical energy in the form of glucose or other sugars.

Chemical Equation

The overall balanced equation for photosynthesis is:

6 CO2 + 6 H2O + Light Energy → C6H12O6 + 6 O2

Key Components

Component Role in Photosynthesis
Chlorophyll Captures light energy
Chloroplasts Site of photosynthesis in plants
Carbon Dioxide (CO2) Raw material for glucose production
Water (H2O) Electron source and raw material

Stages of Photosynthesis

  1. Light Reactions (Light-Dependent Reactions)
    • Takes place in thylakoid membranes
    • Converts light energy to ATP and NADPH
    • Produces oxygen as a byproduct
  2. Calvin Cycle (Light-Independent Reactions)
    • Takes place in the stroma
    • Uses ATP and NADPH from light reactions
    • Converts CO2 to glucose

Factors Affecting Photosynthesis

  • Light intensity - Higher intensity increases rate up to a certain point
  • Carbon dioxide concentration - Higher CO2 levels increase rate
  • Temperature - Optimal temperature range is typically 25-30°C
  • Water availability - Drought reduces photosynthetic rate
  • Chlorophyll content - More chlorophyll allows more light absorption

Importance of Photosynthesis

Photosynthesis is crucial for life on Earth because it:

  • Produces oxygen for respiration
  • Removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere
  • Creates food for plants and indirectly for animals
  • Provides the basis for most food chains
  • Contributes to fossil fuel formation over millions of years
